etymology_story.zh: 教堂义来自中世纪拉丁语 navis，其古典拉丁语本义为“船”，这种命名与教堂主体空间和船形之间的相似联想有关。轮毂义则独立继承自古英语 nafu，与 navel（肚脐）同源，并非由教堂义引申而来。[词源依据：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/nave)
etymology_story.en: The church sense comes from Medieval Latin navis, a specialized use of the Latin word for ship, associated with a perceived resemblance in shape. The wheel sense independently descends from Old English nafu and is related to navel; it did not develop from the church sense. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/nave)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 nave 是不可进一步拆分的单纯词，两种意义属于不同历史来源的同形词；nave + -s → naves（复数）。本词没有常用的直接派生词；nave arcade（中殿拱廊）属于名词组合，naval（海军的）与教堂义有历史词源联系，但不是现代英语中由 nave 加后缀派生的。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, nave is a simple base without productive internal segmentation; its two meanings are historically separate homonyms. Nave + -s gives the plural naves. There are no common direct derivatives; nave arcade is a noun combination, while naval is historically related to the church sense rather than a modern derivative formed from nave.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: main body（主体部分）是教堂义的宽泛释义；central vessel（中央纵向空间）是建筑学中的描述性近义表达；hub（轮毂）只对应车轮义。教堂的 nave 通常区别于两侧的侧廊和用于圣职人员或唱诗班的区域。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Main body is a broad paraphrase of the church sense; central vessel is a descriptive architectural equivalent; hub corresponds only to the wheel sense. A church's nave is normally distinguished from its side aisles and the areas reserved for clergy or the choir.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 教堂义用“船舱般的中央大厅”作记忆图像；轮毂义用“车轮的肚脐”作独立锚点，两条词源分开记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the church nave as a ship-like central hall, and the wheel nave as the wheel's navel. Keep the two historical origins separate.

etymology_story.zh: radial 最终来自拉丁语 radius（辐条、射线），进入英语后表示像射线一样排列或沿半径方向延伸。radius 也用作前臂桡骨的名称，因此 radial 同时发展出解剖学用法；轮胎等名词义则与其径向结构有关。[词源依据：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/radial)
etymology_story.en: Radial ultimately comes from Latin radius, meaning a spoke or ray, and describes arrangements or directions associated with a centre. Because radius also names a forearm bone, radial acquired anatomical uses; nominal applications such as the tyre refer to radial construction. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/radial)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态可分析为 radi-（radius 的词干形式，半径或桡骨）+ -al（……的）；radial + -ly → radially（径向地；放射状地）。直接词族包括 radius（半径；桡骨，复数 radii 或 radiuses）、radial、radially、radials（名词复数）；同源扩展词族包括 radiate（放射）、radiation（辐射）、radiant（光芒四射的）、radiance（光辉）。名词 radial 常由 radial tyre/tire 或 radial engine 省略中心名词形成。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: radi- (the stem of radius, a geometric radius or forearm bone) + -al (relating to); radial + -ly gives radially. The immediate family includes radius, its plurals radii and radiuses, radial, radially, and the noun plural radials. The wider related family includes radiate, radiation, radiant, and radiance. Nominal radial commonly results from shortening radial tyre/tire or radial engine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: radiating（向外放射的）突出从某点延伸；spoke-like（辐条状的）突出外形；centrifugal（离心的）专指背离中心的方向。radial 只说明与半径或中心的几何关系，运动方向既可向外，也可向内。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Radiating emphasizes extension from a point; spoke-like emphasizes appearance; centrifugal specifically indicates movement away from a centre. Radial describes a geometric relationship to a radius or centre and can refer to either inward or outward movement.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: radius 是半径，radial 就是“沿半径的”：车轮辐条、轮胎帘线、星形气缸都围绕中心排列；解剖义另接 radius＝桡骨。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with radius: radial means following a radius. Picture wheel spokes, tyre cords, and engine cylinders arranged around a centre; for anatomy, connect radius with the forearm bone.

etymology_story.zh: bogey 的鬼怪义可能来自 bogle 等方言词，更深层来源并不完全确定。高尔夫用法把预设成绩拟作需要击败的“幽灵对手”，后来固定为高于标准杆一杆；身份未明飞机的用法也与神秘威胁的联想有关。[词源依据：Online Etymology Dictionary](https://www.etymonline.com/word/bogey)
etymology_story.en: The frightening-creature sense probably developed from dialect words such as bogle, although its deeper origin is uncertain. In golf, a target score became an imaginary opponent to defeat and later the score one over par; the unidentified-aircraft use likewise evokes a mysterious potential threat. [Etymological source: Online Etymology Dictionary](https://www.etymonline.com/word/bogey)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代把 bogey 视为不可进一步拆分的词基，不分析为 bog + -ey。名词复数 bogeys；同形转为动词后，第三人称单数 bogeys、过去式及过去分词 bogeyed、现在分词 bogeying；相关复合词有 bogeyman（可怕的人物或事物；吓唬孩子的妖怪，复数 bogeymen）、double bogey（双柏忌）、triple bogey（三柏忌）、bogey-free（未打出柏忌的）。bogie、bogy 是部分名词义的异体拼写，不能在所有语境中随意替换。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat bogey as an unanalyzed modern base, not bog + -ey. Its noun plural is bogeys; conversion produces the verb, with bogeys, bogeyed, and bogeying. Related compounds include bogeyman, plural bogeymen, double bogey, triple bogey, and bogey-free. Bogie and bogy are variant spellings for some noun senses, rather than freely interchangeable forms in every context.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bugbear（令人反复烦恼或恐惧的事物）接近抽象威胁义；phantom（幽灵）接近鬼怪义，但更强调虚幻形体；booger 是鼻屎义的美式口语对应词。高尔夫义有精确的杆数限制，不能用这些词替换。[义项依据：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bogey)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bugbear is close to the persistent worry or threat sense; phantom overlaps with the ghost sense but emphasizes an unreal apparition; booger is the informal American equivalent for nasal mucus. The golf sense has an exact scoring meaning and cannot be replaced by these words. [Sense reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bogey)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 主线记“难缠的幽灵对手”：现实中是令人担忧的威胁，高尔夫中是没能战胜标准杆、反而多打一杆；鼻屎义单独记作英式口语。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use an elusive imaginary opponent as the main anchor: a feared problem in ordinary language, and one stroke worse than par in golf. Learn the British nasal-mucus sense separately.

etymology_story.zh: thatch 的动词可追溯到古英语 theccan，原意为“覆盖”，与德语 decken 和拉丁语 tegere 等表示覆盖的词同源。英语中的含义专门化为用植物材料盖屋顶，并进一步产生屋顶材料、浓密头发和草坪枯草层等名词义。[词源依据：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/thatch)
etymology_story.en: The verb traces back to Old English theccan, meaning to cover, and is related to German decken and Latin tegere. Its English meaning specialized in covering roofs with plant material, alongside noun uses for the covering, thick hair, and accumulated lawn material. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/thatch)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词基为 thatch，兼作名词和动词，没有可继续拆分的常用前后缀。thatch + -er → thatcher（茅草屋顶工）；thatch + -ed → thatched（过去式、过去分词，也可作形容词“茅草覆顶的”）；thatch + -ing → thatching（铺茅草顶；铺顶工艺或材料）；另有 thatches（动词第三人称单数或可数名词复数）、re-thatch/rethatch（重新铺茅草顶）、dethatch（清除草坪枯草层）、dethatcher（枯草层清除机）。
morphology_enriched.en: Thatch is a modern base used as both noun and verb, without a productive internal breakdown. Thatch + -er gives thatcher, a roof craftsperson; + -ed gives thatched, a past form and participial adjective; + -ing gives thatching, the activity, craft, or material. Further forms include thatches, re-thatch/rethatch (cover with thatch again), dethatch (remove lawn thatch), and dethatcher (a machine for removing it).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: straw（秸秆）是一种可用于铺顶的材料，并不等于所有 thatch；roofing（屋面材料）范围更广，包括瓦、金属等；mop（浓密蓬乱的头发）只在头发义上接近 thatch。thatch 的核心是植物材料形成的覆盖层。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Straw is one possible thatching material rather than an equivalent for all thatch; roofing covers a much wider range of materials; mop overlaps only with the thick-hair sense. Thatch centres on a covering or layer formed from plant material.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“厚厚盖上一层”：草盖屋顶是名词 thatch，动手铺草顶是动词 thatch，头发和草坪枯草也能像厚覆盖层。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a thick covering: plant material on a roof is thatch, putting it there is to thatch, and dense hair or lawn debris can resemble the same layer.

senses.meaning_zh: 文具商；文具店经营者；文具销售商
senses.meaning_en: a person or business that sells stationery
senses.english_definition: A stationer is a person or business that sells paper, pens, and other writing or office supplies.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语追溯至盎格鲁法语及中世纪拉丁语中表示固定营业地点的词，与拉丁语 statio（站立处、驻地）有关。它最初指有固定店铺的书商，后来随着经营范围变化，主要指文具商。
etymology_story.en: The word came through Middle English from Anglo-French and Medieval Latin terms associated with a fixed trading location, ultimately related to Latin statio, meaning a standing place or station. It originally referred to a bookseller with a permanent shop and later became associated chiefly with sellers of writing materials.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为完整职业名词学习；词尾 -er 与从业者名词的形式一致，但不宜简单理解为现代 station（车站）加 -er。常用词族：stationer（文具商）、stationers（复数）、stationer's（文具商的；省略 shop 时指文具店）、stationers'（复数所有格）、stationery（文具；历史上由 stationer 派生）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, stationer is usually learned as a complete occupational noun; its ending resembles the occupational suffix -er, although it is not a straightforward formation from modern station. The usual family includes stationer, plural stationers, possessive stationer's, plural possessive stationers', and stationery, historically derived from stationer; stationer's can also stand for stationer's shop.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stationery retailer（文具零售商）是明确、现代的商业表达；office-supply retailer（办公用品零售商）范围更广，也可能销售设备和家具；bookseller（书商）主要销售书籍，属于相关职业而非严格同义词。

etymology_story.zh: 表示地铁的 metro 借自法语 métro，是 métropolitain 的缩略形式，源于表示都市铁路的名称。表示都市圈的形容词用法则是 metropolitan 的缩略形式；这些词最终都与希腊语 mētropolis（母城、大城市）有关。
etymology_story.en: The railway noun was borrowed from French métro, a shortening of métropolitain in the name for a metropolitan railway. The adjective is a shortening of metropolitan; both ultimately connect with Greek mētropolis, meaning a mother city or major city.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词方式为截短：métropolitain 或 metropolitan → metro，而不是英语词根加后缀。常用形式及相关词：metros（地铁系统，复数）、metropolis（大都市）、metropolises（大都市，复数）、metropolitan（大都市的；都市居民）；后三者属于相关词族，并非都直接由 metro 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern formation is clipping: métropolitain or metropolitan becomes metro, rather than an English root taking a suffix. Forms and related words include plural metros, metropolis, plural metropolises, and metropolitan, meaning relating to a major city or an inhabitant of one; the longer words are relatives rather than direct derivatives of metro.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: subway 在美式英语中通常指地铁，但在英式英语中也常指地下人行通道；underground 是英式英语中表示地铁的常用词；metropolitan 对应形容词 metro，语体更正式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Subway usually means an urban underground railway in American English but often means a pedestrian underpass in British English; underground is a common British railway term; metropolitan corresponds to adjectival metro and is more formal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: metropolitan 是“大都市的”：metro 可以指都市里的地铁，也可以修饰整个都市圈。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect metro with metropolitan: it can name the city's railway or describe the wider city area.

etymology_story.zh: 形容词 husky 来自 husk（干燥的外壳）加 -y，早期表示有壳的或像壳一样干涩的，后来出现嗓音粗哑及体格壮实等意义。犬名 husky 则有独立来源，来自与旧称 Eskimo 有关的地区性名称的缩略，并非由形容词直接派生。
etymology_story.en: The adjective was formed from husk plus -y, initially describing something husked or dry like a husk, and later developed the rough-voiced and strongly built senses. The dog name has a separate origin in a shortened regional name connected with the historical term Eskimo, rather than being directly derived from the adjective.

morphology_enriched.zh: 形容词：husk（外壳）+ -y（具有……特征的）→ husky；常用形式为 huskier（更沙哑的；更壮实的）、huskiest（最沙哑的；最壮实的）、huskily（沙哑地）、huskiness（嗓音沙哑；体格壮实）。名词 husky 属于另一词源，复数为 huskies（哈士奇犬）。
morphology_enriched.en: Adjective: husk + -y, meaning having the qualities of, forms husky. Its usual forms are comparative huskier, superlative huskiest, adverb huskily, and noun huskiness, referring to vocal roughness or a sturdy build. The independently derived dog noun has the plural huskies.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hoarse（嘶哑的）更常强调嗓子受损或用嗓过度；raspy（刺耳粗哑的）强调摩擦般的声音，而 husky 可以带有悦耳、富有磁性的意味；burly（魁梧的）对应体格义，强调块头大、身体强壮。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hoarse more often suggests vocal strain or irritation; raspy emphasizes a scratchy sound, whereas husky can describe an attractively low, rough voice; burly matches the physical sense and emphasizes bulk and strength.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 声音义联想干壳摩擦的粗涩感；犬名另记一只拉雪橇的哈士奇，两个来源分开记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the voice, imagine the roughness of a dry husk; remember the separately derived dog name with an image of a sledge-pulling husky.

etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from French secrétariat, referring to a secretary's office or position and later also to the administrative staff collectively. It shares its ancestry with secretary and ultimately Latin secretum, meaning a secret, reflecting the confidential duties of early secretaries.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系可表示为 secretary（秘书；词干变体 secretari-）→ secretariat（秘书处），但该词实际经法语借入。常用词族包括 secretariats（秘书处，复数）、secretary（秘书）、secretaries（秘书，复数）、secretarial（秘书工作的）、secretarially（以秘书工作方式）、secretaryship（秘书职位或任期）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family relationship is secretary, with the stem variant secretari-, to secretariat, although the word itself was borrowed through French. The usual family includes plural secretariats, secretary, plural secretaries, secretarial, secretarially, and secretaryship, meaning the position or tenure of a secretary.

etymology_story.zh: 该词是在近代生命科学发展过程中，由源自希腊语 bios（生命）的构词成分 bio- 与 chemical（化学的）组合而成的科学术语。形容词用于描述生命过程中的化学现象，后来也名词化，用来指相关化学物质。
etymology_story.en: The word developed as a scientific formation combining bio-, from Greek bios meaning life, with chemical as the study of living systems expanded. The adjective describes chemical phenomena in living processes and also became a noun for the substances involved.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bio-（生命、生物）+ chemical（化学的；化学物质）→ biochemical。常用词族：biochemically（在生物化学方面；通过生化过程）、biochemicals（生化物质，复数）、biochemistry（生物化学）、biochemist（生物化学家）、biochemists（生物化学家，复数）；基础相关词有 chemical（化学的；化学物质）、chemically（在化学方面）、chemistry（化学）和 chemist（化学家）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: bio-, meaning life or living organisms, + chemical forms biochemical. The usual family includes biochemically, plural biochemicals, biochemistry, biochemist, and plural biochemists; related base words include chemical, chemically, chemistry, and chemist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chemical（化学的）范围最广，不限于生命系统；biological（生物的）涉及生命现象的各个方面，不专指化学过程；biomolecular（生物分子的）更具体地强调生命活动中的分子及其相互作用，这些词与 biochemical 只有部分重合。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chemical is broader and is not restricted to living systems; biological covers all aspects of life rather than specifically its chemistry; biomolecular focuses more narrowly on biological molecules and their interactions, so these terms overlap only partly with biochemical.

etymology_story.zh: 源自中世纪拉丁语 admissibilis，与拉丁语 admittere（准许进入、接纳）同源；admittere 由 ad-（向）和 mittere（送、放行）构成。“准许进入”的概念后来延伸为允许材料、主张或证据进入正式考虑范围。
etymology_story.en: It comes from Medieval Latin admissibilis, related to Latin admittere, meaning 'let in' or 'accept,' from ad- ('to') and mittere ('send' or 'let go'). The idea of allowing entry developed into allowing material, claims, or evidence to receive formal consideration.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习分析：admiss-（与 admit“接纳”对应的词干变体）+ -ible（可……的）。主要词族：admit（承认；准许进入）、admits（第三人称单数）、admitted（过去式、过去分词）、admitting（现在分词）、admission（承认；准入）、admittance（进入许可）、admissibility（可接受性；证据可采性）、admissibly（以可接受的方式）、inadmissible（不可接受的；不可采纳的）、inadmissibility（不可接受性；不可采性）、inadmissibly（以不可接受的方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern learning analysis: admiss-, a stem variant associated with admit, + -ible ('capable of being'). Main family: admit, admits, admitted, admitting; admission ('acknowledgment or entry'); admittance ('permission to enter'); admissibility; admissibly; inadmissible; inadmissibility; and inadmissibly.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: acceptable（可接受的）范围最广，可指质量或社会规范上令人接受；allowable（规则允许的）强调未超出规定界限；permissible（获准的）强调规则、法律或道德上的许可。admissible 尤其强调是否具备被正式受理或纳入考虑的资格。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Acceptable is broad and may concern quality or social standards; allowable emphasizes remaining within specified limits; permissible emphasizes permission under rules, law, or moral standards. Admissible particularly concerns eligibility for formal acceptance or consideration.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: admit 是“让它进来”；admissible 就是“可以让它进入考虑范围”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Admit means 'let it in'; admissible means 'allowed into consideration.'

senses.meaning_zh: 排泄；排出代谢废物或多余物质
senses.meaning_en: to discharge metabolic waste or excess substances from the body
senses.english_definition: When an organism or an organ excretes a substance, it removes that substance as waste or excess material.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 excernere（筛出、分离）的分词词干 excret-；其中 ex- 表示“向外”，cernere 表示“筛分、分辨”。“分离出去”的含义在生理学中发展为把废物排出体外。
etymology_story.en: It comes from excret-, the participial stem of Latin excernere ('sift out or separate'), formed from ex- ('out') and cernere ('sift or distinguish'). The idea of separating something out developed into the physiological meaning of removing waste from the body.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习分析：ex-（向外）+ -crete（源于拉丁语、表示分离的黏着词干）；不能拆成 ex + create。主要词族：excretes（第三人称单数）、excreted（过去式、过去分词）、excreting（现在分词，去词尾 e 加 -ing）、excretion（排泄；排泄物）、excretory（排泄的）、excretive（有排泄作用的，较少用）；同源词 excreta（排泄物）通常用作复数名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern learning analysis: ex- ('out') + -crete, a bound stem of Latin origin associated with separation; it is not ex + create. Main family: excretes, excreted, excreting (drop final e before -ing), excretion, excretory, and the less common excretive. The related Latin-derived noun excreta ('bodily waste') is normally plural.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: eliminate（排出、清除）范围更广，不专指生理排泄；discharge（排出、释放）强调物质从某处释放出来；egest（排遗）严格指排出未消化的食物残渣。excrete 主要指排出代谢废物或多余物质，与排遗并不完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Eliminate is broader and need not describe a bodily process; discharge emphasizes releasing material from a place; egest specifically means expelling undigested food. Excrete primarily concerns metabolic waste or excess substances and is therefore distinct from egest in technical usage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ex- 是“向外”：把体内不需要的物质分出来、排出去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ex- points outward: separate unwanted material and send it out.

etymology_story.zh: 植物名承自古英语 popig，一般认为最终源自拉丁语 papaver（罂粟）；第一次世界大战战场上的罂粟花使其进一步成为战争纪念象征。音乐形容词则独立由 pop（流行音乐）加 -y 构成，与植物名没有词源关系。
etymology_story.en: The plant name descends from Old English popig and is generally traced ultimately to Latin papaver ('poppy'); poppies on First World War battlefields later helped make the flower a symbol of remembrance. The musical adjective was formed independently from pop ('popular music') + -y and is unrelated to the plant name.

morphology_enriched.zh: 植物名 poppy 在现代英语中是不可进一步拆分的基本词，复数为 poppies（辅音字母加 y 结尾，变 y 为 ies）；常见复合词有 poppy seed／poppyseed（罂粟籽）、poppy-seed oil（罂粟籽油）、poppy field（罂粟花田）。音乐形容词为 pop（流行音乐）+ -y（具有……特点的），双写 p；相关形式有 poppier（更有流行乐风格的）、poppiest（最有流行乐风格的）、poppiness（流行乐风格或上口程度）。
morphology_enriched.en: The plant noun poppy is a simple base in modern English; its plural is poppies, with consonant + y changing to -ies. Common compounds include poppy seed/poppyseed, poppy-seed oil, and poppy field. The musical adjective is pop + -y ('having the qualities of'), with the final p doubled; related forms are poppier, poppiest, and poppiness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 植物义没有适用于所有种类的精确日常近义词：corn poppy（虞美人）和 opium poppy（罂粟）分别指特定种类，不能与泛称 poppy 随意互换。音乐义中，catchy（容易记住、上口的）强调旋律抓耳；poppish（流行乐味较重的）强调风格，较少用；commercial（商业化的）强调市场取向，有时带贬义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The plant sense has no exact everyday synonym covering every kind: corn poppy and opium poppy name particular species rather than interchangeable equivalents of poppy. For music, catchy emphasizes memorable tunes; poppish emphasizes a pop-like style and is less common; commercial emphasizes market appeal and can imply criticism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 植物义：记住“薄花瓣、籽荚、花籽”；音乐义：pop + -y，一听就是流行乐。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the plant, picture delicate petals, a seed capsule, and tiny seeds; for music, pop + -y means 'sounds like pop.'

etymology_story.zh: 源自后期拉丁语 viscosus（黏的），其基础词 viscum 既指槲寄生，也指用其制成的黏鸟胶。“像胶一样黏”的含义后来用于描述流动阻力大的液体。
etymology_story.en: It comes from Late Latin viscosus ('sticky'), based on viscum, meaning both 'mistletoe' and the sticky birdlime made from it. The idea of being glue-like developed into the description of liquids that resist flowing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习分析：visc-（黏性）+ -ous（具有……性质的）。主要词族：viscosity（黏度；黏性）、viscously（黏稠地）、viscousness（黏稠性，较少用）、nonviscous（无黏性的）；相关构词有 viscoelastic（黏弹性的）、viscoelasticity（黏弹性）、viscometer（黏度计）和 viscometry（黏度测定）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern learning analysis: visc- ('stickiness') + -ous ('having the quality of'). Main family: viscosity, viscously, viscousness (less common), and nonviscous. Related formations include viscoelastic, viscoelasticity, viscometer ('an instrument for measuring viscosity'), and viscometry ('viscosity measurement').

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: thick（稠的）是最普通的描述，也可指固体厚度；syrupy（糖浆般黏稠的）突出糖浆般的质感；sticky（黏的）强调容易附着在表面。viscous 更准确地强调液体抵抗流动的性质，并不必然表示容易黏附。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Thick is the everyday term and can also describe the dimensions of solids; syrupy suggests the consistency of syrup; sticky emphasizes adhesion to surfaces. Viscous more precisely describes resistance to flow and does not necessarily imply strong adhesion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象黏鸟胶或蜂蜜慢慢拉丝：越难流动，越 viscous。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture birdlime or honey stretching slowly: greater resistance to flow means more viscous.

etymology_story.zh: 源自后期拉丁语 granulum（小谷粒），是拉丁语 granum（谷粒、颗粒）的指小形式；法语 granule 也参与了这一词形的传播。它从“小谷粒”扩展为各种细小固体颗粒，并用于生物学中的微小颗粒结构。
etymology_story.en: It comes from Late Latin granulum ('a small grain'), a diminutive of Latin granum ('grain'); French granule also helped transmit the form. Its meaning broadened from a little grain to small solid particles generally and to minute structures in biology.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习分析：gran-（颗粒、谷粒）+ -ule（小的）；这一拆分反映历史构词，现代英语通常把 granule 作为完整基本词使用。主要词族：granules（复数）、granular（颗粒状的；细致的）、granularity（粒度；细化程度）、granulate（使成粒；形成颗粒）、granulates（第三人称单数）、granulated（过去式、过去分词；颗粒状的）、granulating（现在分词）、granulation（成粒；肉芽形成）、granulator（造粒机）；相关专业词有 granulocyte（粒细胞）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern learning analysis: gran- ('grain') + -ule ('small'); this reflects the historical formation, while modern English generally treats granule as a complete base. Main family: granules, granular ('grain-like or detailed'), granularity ('grain size or level of detail'), granulate, granulates, granulated, granulating, granulation, and granulator ('a machine that forms granules'). A related technical term is granulocyte ('a white blood cell containing granules').

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grain（粒）常指谷粒或盐、沙等物质的一粒；particle（微粒）范围最广，可指极微小的固体或其他物质单位；pellet（小丸、颗粒）通常指压制或形成的较规则小块。granule 强调细小、可分辨的颗粒，常见于粉粒状材料和生物学描述。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grain often means a cereal seed or a single piece of salt, sand, or a similar substance; particle is broader and can describe extremely small units of matter; pellet usually suggests a compact, often deliberately formed piece. Granule emphasizes a small, distinct grain, especially in granular materials and biological descriptions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gran- 是“粒”，-ule 是“小”：granule 就是“一小粒”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Gran- means 'grain' and -ule means 'small': a granule is a little grain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再按常用词缀拆分的单纯词 spire。主要词形及派生词：spires（名词复数）、spired（有尖塔的，常用于复合形容词）、spire-like／spirelike（尖塔状的）。

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: steeple（教堂塔楼，常包括尖顶及其下方塔身）、pinnacle（建筑物上的小尖顶或装饰性尖塔）、tower（塔，顶部不一定尖）。spire 特别强调细长、向上收尖的形状。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A steeple is a church tower, often including its pointed top; a pinnacle is a smaller architectural point or ornamental turret; a tower need not have a pointed top. Spire specifically emphasizes a tall, tapering shape.

senses.meaning_zh: 使脱离；公开撇清与某人、组织或观点的关系
senses.meaning_en: to distance oneself from a person, group, or opinion
senses.english_definition: If you dissociate yourself from someone or something, you make it clear that you are not connected with them or do not support them.

senses.sentence_zh: 她公开表示自己不赞同该团体的观点。

senses.meaning_zh: 把相互关联的事物分开考虑；割裂
senses.meaning_en: to separate things that are connected, especially in thought
senses.english_definition: If you dissociate one thing from another, you consider or treat them as separate even though they are connected.
senses.collocation_en: dissociate art from politics; dissociate the individual from society

senses.meaning_zh: 〔化学〕解离，使分解为较小的粒子
senses.meaning_en: to separate into smaller chemical particles, or cause this to happen
senses.english_definition: When a substance dissociates, it separates into smaller particles such as ions, atoms, or molecules.
senses.collocation_en: dissociate into ions; dissociate in solution
senses.collocation_zh: 解离成离子；在溶液中解离
senses.sentence_en: Acetic acid partially dissociates into ions in water.
senses.sentence_zh: 乙酸在水中部分解离成离子。

senses.meaning_zh: 〔心理学〕产生解离，与自身感受、记忆或周围环境脱节
senses.meaning_en: to become mentally disconnected from feelings, memories, or surroundings
senses.english_definition: If someone dissociates, they experience a mental separation from their feelings, memories, sense of identity, or surroundings.
senses.collocation_en: dissociate during stress; dissociate from painful memories
senses.collocation_zh: 在压力下产生解离；与痛苦记忆发生心理脱离
senses.sentence_en: During periods of intense stress, she sometimes dissociates and feels detached from her surroundings.
senses.sentence_zh: 在承受强烈压力时，她有时会产生解离，感觉自己与周围环境脱节。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 dissociāre，意为“拆散、使分离”，由 dis-（分开）与 sociāre（联合）构成，后者与 socius（同伴）有关。“拆开联系”的核心意义后来用于公开划清关系、化学解离和心理解离。
etymology_story.en: Dissociate comes from Latin dissociāre, meaning to separate, formed from dis- (apart) and sociāre (to join), related to socius (companion). Its central idea of breaking a connection later extended to public distancing, chemical separation, and psychological disconnection.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 dis-（分离）+ soci-（同伴、联结的拉丁来源词干）+ -ate（动词构形成分）；这不是把现代 associate 直接加上 dis-，后者形成另一个词 disassociate。主要词族：dissociates（第三人称单数）、dissociated（过去式、过去分词；脱离的）、dissociating（现在分词）、dissociation（分离；解离）、dissociative（解离的）、dissociable（可分离的）。相关同源词包括 associate（联系；同伴）、association（联系；协会）和 social（社会的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The learned structure is dis- (apart) + soci- (a Latin-derived stem associated with companionship or joining) + -ate (a verb-forming element). It is not simply dis- added to modern associate, which produces the separate word disassociate. Principal family members are dissociates, dissociated (past tense, past participle, and an adjective meaning disconnected), dissociating, dissociation (separation), dissociative (involving dissociation), and dissociable (capable of separation). Related cognates include associate, association, and social.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: separate（最通用的“分开”，可指实际或抽象分离）、detach（强调解除附着或情感牵连）、disavow（明确否认支持、责任或关联）。dissociate 强调切断或否认联系；化学和心理学用法通常不能直接换成 disavow。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Separate is the broadest term for making things distinct; detach emphasizes removing an attachment or emotional connection; disavow explicitly rejects support, responsibility, or association. Dissociate focuses on breaking or denying a connection, and its chemical and psychological uses generally cannot be replaced by disavow.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: soci- 表示“联结”，dis- 把联结拆开：关系、粒子或心理体验都可因此分离。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of soci- as a connection and dis- as pulling it apart: relationships, particles, or mental experiences become separated.

etymology_story.zh: 由英语 up（向上）和 turn（转动、转变）组合而成，字面意思是“向上转”。这一空间动作后来也用来表示经济、销售等从低迷转向增长。
etymology_story.en: Upturn combines the English words up and turn, literally expressing an upward movement or change of direction. This physical image also developed into a term for improvement in business, sales, and economic conditions.

morphology_enriched.zh: up + turn → upturn，是可作名词或动词的复合词。主要词形及派生形式：upturns（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、upturned（过去式、过去分词；朝上的、翻转的）、upturning（现在分词）。相关复合词有 downturn（衰退、下降）；短语 turn up 与 upturn 的用法并不相同。
morphology_enriched.en: Up + turn forms the compound upturn, used as both a noun and a verb. Principal forms are upturns (plural noun or third-person singular verb), upturned (past tense, past participle, and an adjective meaning facing upward or overturned), and upturning (present participle). A related compound is downturn (a decline). The phrasal verb turn up has its own distinct uses.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: improvement（广义的改善，不一定涉及数量增长）、recovery（从衰退或损失中恢复）、upswing（较明显的上升势头）。upturn 常指趋势开始转好，未必已经完全恢复。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Improvement broadly means becoming better without necessarily increasing in quantity; recovery means returning from a decline or loss; upswing suggests a more noticeable upward movement. An upturn often marks a change toward better conditions without implying a complete recovery.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: up + turn：曲线拐头向上，就是“回升”；把脸向上转，就是“仰起”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Up + turn: a graph turns upward in an improvement, and a face turns upward when it is raised.

senses.meaning_zh: 字节，现代计算机中通常由八个二进制位组成的数据单位
senses.meaning_en: a unit of digital information normally consisting of eight bits
senses.english_definition: A byte is a unit of digital information that normally consists of eight bits.
senses.collocation_en: a byte of data; bytes of memory
senses.collocation_zh: 一个字节的数据；以字节计的内存容量
senses.sentence_en: This file contains exactly 256 bytes of data.

etymology_story.zh: 计算机工程师 Werner Buchholz 于1956年创造了 byte 一词，将 bite（咬下的一口）改拼，以免与 bit 混淆。早期一个 byte 所含的位数并不固定，后来八位字节成为通行标准。
etymology_story.en: Computer engineer Werner Buchholz coined byte in 1956 as a respelling of bite designed to avoid confusion with bit. Early bytes could contain different numbers of bits, but the eight-bit byte later became standard.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 byte 是不可再拆分的技术名词，历史上来自 bite 的改拼。主要词形及构词成员：bytes（复数）、kilobyte（千字节）、megabyte（兆字节）、gigabyte（吉字节）、terabyte（太字节）；二进制计量词包括 kibibyte（1024字节）和 mebibyte（1024个kibibyte）。常见派生及复合形式有 bytewise（逐字节的／地）、multibyte（多字节的）和 bytecode（字节码）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, byte is an indivisible technical noun, historically created by respelling bite. Its plural is bytes, and major prefixed forms include kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte, and terabyte. Binary measurement terms include kibibyte (1,024 bytes) and mebibyte (1,024 kibibytes). Common derivatives and compounds include bytewise (one byte at a time), multibyte (involving multiple bytes), and bytecode (a form of encoded program instructions).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: octet（严格指八位的一组，网络协议中常用）、bit（二进制位，单个0或1）、word（机器字，处理器按整体处理的数据单位，其大小依架构而定）。octet 是最接近的术语；bit 和 word 是相关单位，并非 byte 的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Octet means exactly eight bits and is common in networking; bit means a single binary digit; word means a data unit handled as a whole by a processor, with a size that depends on the architecture. Octet is the closest equivalent, while bit and word are related units rather than synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 byte 想成“一口数据”：现代计算机通常一口装八个 bit。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine a byte as one bite of data: in modern computing, that bite normally holds eight bits.

senses.meaning_en: a flat geometric shape with five straight sides and five angles
senses.english_definition: A pentagon is a flat shape that has five straight sides and five angles.
senses.collocation_en: a regular pentagon; an irregular pentagon
senses.collocation_zh: 正五边形；不规则五边形
senses.sentence_en: Draw a regular pentagon with five equal sides.
senses.sentence_zh: 画一个五条边等长的正五边形。

senses.meaning_zh: 〔the Pentagon〕五角大楼；美国国防部或其领导层
senses.meaning_en: the headquarters of the US Department of Defense, or the department's leadership
senses.english_definition: The Pentagon is the headquarters of the US Department of Defense, and the name is also used to refer to the department or its leaders.
senses.collocation_en: Pentagon officials; a Pentagon spokesperson
senses.collocation_zh: 美国国防部官员；美国国防部发言人
senses.sentence_en: A Pentagon spokesperson answered questions about the military exercise.
senses.sentence_zh: 美国国防部一名发言人回答了有关此次军事演习的问题。

etymology_story.zh: 经法语和拉丁语传入英语，最终源自希腊语中表示“五角的”形式，其成分与 pente（五）和 gōnia（角）有关。美国国防部总部因建筑平面呈五边形而称为 the Pentagon，这个名称又转用于指该部门及其领导层。
etymology_story.en: Pentagon entered English through French and Latin and ultimately comes from a Greek form meaning five-angled, related to pente (five) and gōnia (angle). The US defense headquarters was named the Pentagon for its five-sided plan, and the name also came to represent the department and its leadership.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词结构为 penta-（五）+ -gon（多边形构词成分，历史义为“角”）→ pentagon。主要词形及派生词：pentagons（复数）、pentagonal（五边形的）、pentagonally（呈五边形地）。大写形式 Pentagon 用于专名；相关构词有 pentagram（五角星形）和 hexagon（六边形），二者不是 pentagon 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern learned structure is penta- (five) + -gon (a combining form used in polygon names, historically referring to angles). Principal forms and derivatives are pentagons (plural), pentagonal (having five sides), and pentagonally (in a five-sided arrangement). Capitalized Pentagon is a proper name. Related formations include pentagram (a five-pointed star) and hexagon (a six-sided polygon), neither of which is a derivative of pentagon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: five-sided polygon（五边多边形，是几何义的直接释义）、regular pentagon（正五边形，边长与内角分别相等，是其子类）、pentagram（五角星形，与五边形不同）。专名 Pentagon 可借代美国国防部，但这种替换依语境而定。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Five-sided polygon is a direct equivalent of the geometric sense; regular pentagon is a subtype with equal sides and equal interior angles; pentagram is a five-pointed star and is a different figure. As a proper name, Pentagon can stand for the US Department of Defense, depending on context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: penta- 是“五”，-gon 提示“角”：五个角围成五边形，也解释了五角大楼的名称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Penta- means five and -gon points to angles: five corners form a pentagon and explain the Pentagon's name.
